summary: Frontend-only regression + new-feature verification (Finance Deep Dive + Tariff History). All 8 requested checks pass. 4-step flow renders res-net-benefit ₹2,82,820, no NaN/Infinity/undefined anywhere on results page. Finance Deep Dive card 'Financing — full breakdown' shows payoff banner 'You pay ₹4,49,293/month for 84 months from Sept 2026 until Sept 2033' (84 = tenure 7yr × 12 ✅). Toggle finance-method to Flat rate: red pill 'Effective rate ≈ 14.4% reducing' vs quoted flat 8.5% → 1.69× ratio, cleanly within the expected 1.6–1.9× band. Fee breakdown rows all populated with rupee values (Project cost ₹3.28 Cr, Down payment ₹65.60 L, Loan ₹2.62 Cr, Processing fee 1% ₹2,62,400, GST 18% ₹47,232, Insurance 0.35% ₹1,14,800, Total upfront ₹69,84,432). Repayment metrics render (EMI ₹4,49,293, Total Interest ₹1.15 Cr, Total Repayment ₹3.77 Cr, Total Cost of Credit ₹1.19 Cr, Payoff Sept 2033). Reducing-vs-flat comparison table shows both rows with effective rate for flat. EMI schedule (toggle-schedule): 7 yearly rows; Year 1 interest ₹27.56 L > principal ₹26.35 L (interest-heavy ✅); Year 7 closing balance = ₹0 ✅. Tariff History card: 10-yr line chart 2016→2026, Haryana default shows 10-yr CAGR 4.0%, 5-yr 4.4%, ₹5.34 (2016) → ₹7.90 (2026), risers grid with Maharashtra 5.2% at top ✅. Edit/Recalc: switching to Maharashtra + MSEDCL auto-fills tariff to ₹11 (green banner confirms), re-running produces tariff history with 10-yr CAGR 5.2% / 5-yr 5.6%, ₹6.63 (2016) → ₹11 (2026), Maharashtra highlighted (amber border) in the risers grid.
critical_code_review_comments: FinanceDeepDive is a self-contained useMemo island — nice. Consider surfacing feePct/flatRate back to the parent lead payload so submitted leads reflect any user tweaks; today the lead uses model.loan (defaults) only. Non-blocking.

buildTariffHistory uses new Date().getFullYear() so labels drift automatically over time — good. But firstYr label 2016 is derived not sourced; the SourceTag already carries 'Indicative' — acceptable.
topTariffRisers iterates STATES which is fine; if a future state code is missing from TARIFF_CAGR it falls back to DEFAULT_CAGR (4.0%). No crash risk.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New testids introduced in FinanceDeepDive: finance-method (Segmented, options: 'Reducing rate' | 'Flat rate'), fee-slider (0–3%, step 0.25), flat-slider (only visible on Flat method, 5–13%, step 0.25), toggle-schedule (button). Payoff months = tenureYears*12 (7*12=84 default). Effective-rate check: for flatRate=8.5%, tenure=7y, principal≈₹2.62 Cr → effective ≈14.4% (~1.69x). TariffHistory reads getStateByName(f.state)?.code and looks up TARIFF_CAGR — Maharashtra (MH) 5.2%/5.6%, Haryana (HR) 4.0%/4.4% (falls to DEFAULT since HR is 4.0/4.4 — coincidence). Risers list is sorted by c10 desc. To reach results: load-demo-btn → 4x calc-next-btn. To edit state: click 'Edit inputs' button (uses page.get_by_role) then click step-tab-1 to go back to Location. Everything green — no known bugs remaining.
